release_notes: Configuration discovery now accepts both docsentinel.toml and doc_sentinel.toml as the standalone config file; docsentinel.toml remains the preferred name.
Having both standalone files in one scan root is ambiguous and fails closed with a ConfigError (exit code 2) naming both files.
`docsentinel init` still creates docsentinel.toml but refuses to run next to an existing doc_sentinel.toml.
Documentation updated (configuration reference, tutorials, architecture, README) and new unit, integration and mock tests cover both names.
First stable release of DocSentinel, a deterministic-first documentation QA framework and Python library with one engine behind the CLI, the Python API and the pytest plugin.

Fast profile (stdlib only): DS101 dangling links/anchors, DS102 stray HTML comments, DS103 unresolvable path-like code spans, DS104 conflicting heading/explicit anchors, DS105 heading hierarchy, DS106 empty sections, DS108 reference-style link integrity, DS109 malformed/unclosed code fences, DS113 missing local assets, DS114 duplicate document identifiers, DS116 path traversal outside the documentation root, DS117 malformed GFM tables.

Opt-in policy rules, inert until configured: DS110 fence language labels (require_fence_languages), DS112 navigation integrity (navigation_indexes), DS115 deprecated names and migrated references (deprecated_references_file), DS118 file and directory naming (documentation_naming).

Standard profile (docsentinel[standard]): DS201 text complexity, DS202 duplicated text, DS203 low-information content, DS204 docstring-to-signature mismatch, with separate baseline and CI lanes and lazy loading of heavy dependencies.

Deep profile (docsentinel[deep]): DS301 fact-contradiction candidates; heuristic, advisory-only (exit code 0) and gated behind an explicit opt-in (deep_confirm, --i-understand-deep-is-heuristic or DOCSENTINEL_DEEP_CONFIRM=1).
Layered configuration via doc_sentinel.toml or [tool.doc_sentinel] in pyproject.toml, with typed and validated policy options, rule selection by code or prefix, and SHA-256 fingerprint baselines.

CLI commands scan, baseline, init, rules and doctor; text, JSON (schema v1) and GitHub Actions output; exit codes 0 (clean), 1 (blocking findings), 2 (config or scan failure); pre-commit hooks for the fast and standard profiles.
Security hardening: control, bidi and zero-width characters are neutralised in text and GitHub annotation output, and path handling is contained to the scan root with symlink-escape protection.
Packaging: release tooling (release-saga) and flakeforge are declared as dependencies; wheels and sdists are built with hatchling and requires Python 3.12+.
